sentences.text: Kentisuchus is a member of the parent group Gavialoidea.
Recent molecular studies indicate that Tomistominae, including extinct forms like Kentisuchus, belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
William Buckland named Crocodylus spenceri based on a partial skull found on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, England.
Charles Mook erected the genus Kentisuchus in 1955 for the species originally described by Richard Owen in 1849.
Research suggests Kentisuchus dispersed from mainland Europe to islands in the Tethysian archipelago rather than migrating from Africa.
Kentisuchus lived between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
Fossils of Kentisuchus have been found in England and France dating to the early Eocene.
Kentisuchus has been recorded from Ukraine, though it is unclear if those specimens belong to the genus.
